edges.description: Loss of cycling progenitors collapses marrow output.
Suppressed marrow output empties the peripheral blood of all lineages.
Lymphocytes fall first, within hours of exposure.
Loss of neutrophils and platelets produces the infections and bleeding that drive mortality.
Neutropenia removes the principal defence against bacterial infection.
The radiation exposure is the physical insult that initiates progenitor killing.
Reproduces the marrow suppression and its survival consequence at a controlled dose, which is what allows countermeasure efficacy to be measured at all.
edges.limitations: Dose is uniform, delivered by linear accelerator, and paired with protocolised supportive care. A human casualty has an unknown, non-uniform dose and variable care, so the dose-equivalence assumption is the part that does not transfer cleanly.

nodes.description: A single high-dose exposure from a criticality accident, radiological source mishandling, reactor accident or nuclear detonation. It is distinguished from therapeutic irradiation by being uncontrolled, unfractionated, and usually of initially unknown dose, which is what makes early triage on lymphocyte depletion kinetics necessary.

evidence.reference_title: Radiation countermeasures for hematopoietic acute radiation syndrome: growth factors, cytokines and beyond.
evidence.snippet: It is critical that additional agents for other major sub-syndromes of ARS (gastrointestinal-ARS) be approved.

nodes.description: Marrow aplasia following radiation injury to the progenitor pool. Unlike the predictable nadir-and-recovery of a chemotherapy cycle, the depth and reversibility here are set by a single uncontrolled exposure, so the clinical question is whether enough stem cells survived to permit autologous recovery.

animal_models.name: Non-human primate total-body irradiation model

nodes.description: Neutropenic infection and haemorrhage are the proximate causes of death in the haematopoietic subsyndrome, and they are what supportive care and growth factors are given to prevent. Kept separate from the cytopenias themselves because the countermeasures act on the counts while the mortality is driven by the complications.

evidence.reference_title: Filgrastim improves survival in lethally irradiated nonhuman primates.
evidence.snippet: Filgrastim, administered at this dose and schedule, effectively mitigated the lethality of the hematopoietic subsyndrome of the acute radiation syndrome.

nodes.description: Lymphopenia is the earliest and most useful haematological sign, because lymphocytes are exquisitely radiosensitive and fall within hours. The rate of the fall over the first 48 hours is the basis of early biodosimetry triage when the physical dose is unknown.

Filgrastim is FDA-approved for the haematopoietic subsyndrome and acts by stimulating surviving myeloid progenitors to accelerate granulocyte recovery. It shortens the duration of neutropenia without altering the nadir, so it rescues marrow output rather than preventing the initial radiation injury.

evidence.reference_title: Filgrastim improves survival in lethally irradiated nonhuman primates.
evidence.snippet: Filgrastim significantly (P < 0.004) reduced 60 day overall mortality [20.8% (5/24)] compared to the controls [59.1% (13/22)].

nodes.description: Penetrating ionizing radiation delivered to the whole body over a short period kills proliferating haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in the marrow. The marrow is the first compartment to fail because its progenitors are the most rapidly cycling, which is the same reason it is the dose-limiting tissue for cytotoxic chemotherapy - the insult differs but the vulnerable cell population does not.

evidence.reference_title: Radiation countermeasures for hematopoietic acute radiation syndrome: growth factors, cytokines and beyond.
evidence.snippet: These agents are largely recombinant growth factors (e.g. rhuG-CSF/filgrastim, rhuGM-CSF/sargramostim) that target and stimulate myeloid progenitors within bone marrow.

nodes.description: Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia and anaemia appear in sequence set by each lineage's circulating half-life, with lymphocytes falling first and fastest. Duration of neutropenia rather than nadir depth is the parameter the approved countermeasures actually shift.

evidence.reference_title: Filgrastim improves survival in lethally irradiated nonhuman primates.
evidence.snippet: Filgrastim significantly decreased the duration of neutropenia, but did not affect the absolute neutrophil count nadir.

nodes.description: Rhesus macaques given a mid-lethal total-body dose with protocol-defined supportive care. This is the model the entire approved-countermeasure evidence base rests on, and under the FDA Animal Rule it is the model that stands in for the human efficacy trial that cannot be run.
Neutropenic infection, the proximate cause of death in the haematopoietic subsyndrome.
A thrombopoietin receptor agonist approved for the haematopoietic subsyndrome, addressing the platelet lineage that growth-factor support for granulocytes does not cover.

evidence.reference_title: Radiation countermeasures for hematopoietic acute radiation syndrome: growth factors, cytokines and beyond.
evidence.snippet: Romiplostim, a small molecular agonist that enhances platelet production via stimulation of bone marrow megakaryocytes, has been recently approved and indicated for H-ARS.

nodes.description: Recombinant GM-CSF, also FDA-approved for the haematopoietic subsyndrome. It acts on the same surviving-progenitor pool as filgrastim but across a broader myeloid range, and is stockpiled alongside it.
